ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, there is a larger outer equilateral triangle, and inside there is a smaller equilateral triangle. Three congruent triangles are arranged in a spiral around the inner equilateral triangle; each side of the outer triangle appears to be one side of one of the triangles. At the vertices of the inner equilateral triangle, an angle of a surrounding triangle is adjacent to the inner 60° angle, forming a straight-line supplementary-angle relationship. The figure also shows the collinear relationship of the spiral: some line segments are composed of one side length of the inner equilateral triangle plus a segment of the adjacent small triangle's side. Reasoning: Denote the outer equilateral triangle as ABC, and the inner equilateral triangle as PQR. Look at the inner vertex P; the angle of the inner equilateral triangle is 60°, and the angle of an adjacent triangle at P is supplementary to it, so that angle is 120°. The side lengths of triangle T are 1, 2, sqrt(7). By the law of cosines, if 120° is between sides 1 and 2, then the opposite side length satisfies c^2=1^2+2^2-2·1·2·cos120°=1+4+2=7, so c=sqrt(7). Therefore the side opposite the 120° angle in this triangle, namely one side of the outer equilateral triangle, has length sqrt(7). Next look at the collinear spiral structure in the figure: the two sides adjacent to the 120° angle in one triangle can be regarded as having lengths y and y+s respectively, where s is the side length of the inner equilateral triangle, and y is the length of the adjacent connecting segment. They must correspond to the two shorter sides 1 and 2 of triangle T. Because y+s>y, y=1 and y+s=2, hence s=1. Therefore the side length of the inner equilateral triangle is 1, and the side length of the outer equilateral triangle is sqrt(7). The area ratio of equilateral triangles is equal to the square of the side-length ratio, so the area ratio is (sqrt(7)/1)^2=7.

It turns out that one can arrange three copies of triangle $T$ to form two equilateral triangles, one inside the other, as shown below. method.method_draft: First read the image by labeling the outer equilateral triangle as ABC and the inner equilateral triangle as PQR, with the three copies of T spiraling around the inner triangle. At an inner vertex such as P, the side of the surrounding copy continues along two sides of the inner equilateral, so the angle of that copy at P is supplementary to the 60° inner-equilateral angle, hence 120°. From the text, T has sides 1, 2, and sqrt(7); by the law of cosines, the 120° angle is between the sides 1 and 2 and is opposite the side sqrt(7). Therefore the outer side AB of the large equilateral triangle is sqrt(7). Next use the visual collinearity in the spiral: one side of a surrounding copy is a straight segment made of one inner-equilateral side plus the corresponding short side of the next congruent copy. Thus if the connector length is y and the inner side is s, the two sides adjacent to the 120° angle are y and y+s, which must be 1 and 2. Since y+s>y, get y=1 and s=1. The ratio of areas of equilateral triangles is the square of the ratio of side lengths, so the required ratio is (sqrt(7)/1)^2=7.

图像描述：附图中有一个较大的外部等边三角形，内部有一个较小的等边三角形。三份全等三角形围绕内部等边三角形呈螺旋状排列；外部三角形的每一条边看起来都是某一份三角形的一条边。内部等边三角形的顶点处，周围三角形的一条角与内部的60°角相邻，形成一条直线补角关系。图中还显示出螺旋的共线关系：某些直线段由一个内部等边三角形边长加上相邻小三角形的一段边组成。

推理：把外部等边三角形记为ABC，内部等边三角形记为PQR。看内部顶点P处，内部等边三角形的角是60°，而相邻的一份三角形在P处的角与它互补，所以该角为120°。三角形T的边长为1、2、sqrt(7)。由余弦定理，若120°夹在边1和边2之间，则对边长度满足 c^2=1^2+2^2-2·1·2·cos120°=1+4+2=7，所以 c=sqrt(7)。因此这份三角形中120°角的对边，即外部等边三角形的一条边，长度为sqrt(7)。

再看图中的共线螺旋结构：一份三角形中与120°角相邻的两条边，可以看成长度分别为y和y+s，其中s是内部等边三角形的边长，y是相邻连接段的长度。它们必须对应三角形T的两条较短边1和2。因为y+s>y，所以y=1，y+s=2，从而s=1。因此内部等边三角形边长为1，外部等边三角形边长为sqrt(7)。等边三角形面积比等于边长比的平方，所以面积比为 (sqrt(7)/1)^2=7。

The area of one copy of T is (1/2)(1)(2)sin120°=sqrt(3)/2, so the three surrounding copies have total area 3sqrt(3)/2. Since the image shows these copies are exactly the region between the two equilateral triangles, inner area = outer area - 3 area(T) = 7sqrt(3)/4 - 3sqrt(3)/2 = sqrt(3)/4. Therefore the side opposite the 120° angle in this triangle, namely one side of the outer equilateral triangle, has length sqrt(7).

Next look at the collinear spiral structure in the figure: the two sides adjacent to the 120° angle in one triangle can be regarded as having lengths y and y+s respectively, where s is the side length of the inner equilateral triangle, and y is the length of the adjacent connecting segment. They must correspond to the two shorter sides 1 and 2 of triangle T. Because y+s>y, y=1 and y+s=2, hence s=1. Therefore the side length of the inner equilateral triangle is 1, and the side length of the outer equilateral triangle is sqrt(7). The area ratio of equilateral triangles is equal to the square of the side-length ratio, so the area ratio is (sqrt(7)/1)^2=7.
